body:
GitHub issue #365. This is #326 F4 ("revision binds tree not diff", ADR-0007) biting
repeatedly in practice. NOT the same as #355 (F1, truncation).

## Problem

`resolveRevision` (`packages/core/lib/revision.mjs`) hashes EVERY tracked and untracked file
minus `ignorePaths`. An attestation therefore binds to the whole worktree, not to the change
that was reviewed. Any advance of `main` invalidates an attestation for a change that has not
moved.

## Evidence (#362, 2026-07-27)

1. Attestation recorded and green for revision `git-worktree:71c7050a...`.
2. Branch rebased onto newer main, picking up ONE commit — #361 (Copilot integration docs,
   marketing facts, `plugins/adlc-herdr/package.json`). No interaction with the reviewed code.
3. Revision moved to `a42b9cf8...`; the `gate` check went red.
4. The reviewed change was BYTE-FOR-BYTE identical — verified mechanically: the cumulative
   diff of the three changed files against the merge-base was 12950 bytes before and after the
   rebase, `diff` reporting no difference.

A fully reviewed, unchanged change was rejected because someone merged documentation. Per the
prior handoff notes, main advanced ~4 times during #314, invalidating the attestation each time.

## Why this matters beyond the annoyance

The cost is what the treadmill TEACHES. Facing a red gate on an unchanged, already-reviewed
diff, the tempting moves are (a) re-record without re-reviewing, making the attestation a
rubber stamp, or (b) drop the attestation and admin-override. The previous handoff document
recommended (b) as standard practice: "Unless you can rebase+re-record+merge within one quiet
window, just drop the attestation and admin-override." Both hollow out the gate — the same
erosion pattern as the session-lifetime ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS in #162/#204. A mechanism whose
correct use is impractical trains people out of using it correctly.

## Design — DECIDED: A+B (maintainer, 2026-07-27)

The two halves are NOT independent. Recording `base_sha` is what makes the binding sound, but it
is ALSO what keeps the treadmill alive: a rebase changes `base_sha`, so the attestation goes stale
again — the same defect wearing a new field. What survives base movement is the DIFF hash alone,
and matching on the diff hash alone is unsound (a diff reviewed against base X can be wrong
against base Y — a semantic conflict the reviewer never saw).

So: **A supplies the soundness, B makes it affordable.**

**A — bind to `(base_sha, change_set_hash)`.**
Attestation identity becomes the pair, not a hash of the whole worktree. `change_set_hash` covers
the reviewed change only, so unrelated files elsewhere in the tree cannot invalidate it. Recording
`base_sha` keeps "reviewed against WHAT" auditable.

**CORRECTED 2026-07-28 — the basis is `base` → WORKING TREE, tracked paths only.** A first build
bound the identity to `base..HEAD` (committed only) and refused on a dirty tree. It was reverted:
it silently broke a deliberate capability.
`packages/prosecute/test/prosecute-cross-model-cli.test.mjs` — `FIX A: an UNCOMMITTED edit to a
trust-root file tiers (invisible to a committed three-dot diff)` — proves this codebase's
prosecution model is WORKING-TREE-INCLUSIVE on purpose. A committed-only identity would describe
something the gate does not prosecute. That is a fail-open, not a simplification.

Per changed tracked path, hash `(path, base_mode, base_blob_sha, current_mode, current_blob_sha)`:

- **BASE side** read from the tree object (`git diff --raw` src fields).
- **CURRENT side COMPUTED from the working tree, never read from `git diff --raw`.** For an
  unstaged modification `--raw` reports `dstsha` as all zeros, so reading it collapses every
  distinct working-tree content to one identity — a collision.
- **Untracked excluded**, matching classification: `changedFiles` reads `git diff`, which ignores
  untracked. See Decision 2 and the honest limit below for what this does and does not cover.

Side benefit worth stating: today's whole-worktree hash includes UNTRACKED files
(`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` in resolveRevision), which is why a local revision
diverges from CI's clean checkout whenever scratch files are present — a real trap hit twice
already. The change set has no untracked term, so local and CI agree by construction.

**B — explicit, auditable carry-forward.**
A first-class operation for "base moved, diff did not". It must COMPUTE that the diff hash is
unchanged rather than take the author's word, record the new `base_sha`, and link to the prior
verdict so the ledger shows a verdict was CARRIED rather than freshly earned. This is exactly the
manual dance performed by hand on #362 and #367 (verify the diff is byte-identical, run a
confirmatory review, re-record); B makes it a supported operation instead of a full review round
each time main moves.

**C is rejected.** Narrowing the whole-tree hash without recording the base loses "reviewed
against what" entirely — it trades one soundness problem for another.

## Open questions — BOTH DECIDED (maintainer, 2026-07-28)

**Decision 1 — is there also a committed-only (`base..HEAD`) mode? NO.** Only the
working-tree-inclusive form exists. Rationale: (a) two forms are the accept-either-form shape F4
warns about, and any ambiguity about which one the gate computed is a bypass; (b) prosecution is
working-tree-inclusive, so a committed-only identity would describe something the gate does not
prosecute; (c) asymmetric reversibility — adding a second form later is additive (new prefix, its
own matching rule), whereas removing one from a populated append-only ledger is not.

**Decision 2 — untracked files during prosecution: REFUSE now, file execution isolation
separately.** Refuse when untracked-and-NOT-ignored files are present. **CRITICAL SCOPING: the
check must NOT trigger on gitignored files.** `node_modules` is gitignored and always present, so
refusing on it would brick prosecution permanently. Measured friction for the rule as scoped: **0**
untracked-not-ignored files across both checkouts — the friction objection had no data behind it.
See the honest limit below for what this does not cover.

### Compatibility constraint (discovered while landing #364)

`main` already carries THREE signed attestations in `git-worktree:<sha256>` form (seq 96, 97 from
 #362, and 98 from #367). The gate MUST keep honouring those, or every historical attestation is
invalidated at once and the ledger's existing evidence is worthless. The new scheme therefore has
to coexist with the old during a transition, not replace it.


## P1 premortem — findings and the hardening they force (2026-07-27)

Five concrete failure mechanisms. All are now binding design constraints, not advice.

**F1 — carry-forward becomes a rubber stamp.** A diff can be byte-identical and semantically
WRONG against a new base (main renames a helper it calls, or tightens a validator it relies on).
If B is cheap and A is strict, operators reach for B reflexively and a verdict rides forward over
bases nobody examined — worse than the treadmill, which at least forced a fresh look.
DECIDED (maintainer): **cap the chain at N=3 carry-forwards**, then the gate demands a fresh
distinct-provider review. The ledger records chain DEPTH so the Nth-hand status is auditable.

**F2 — `git diff` TEXT is the wrong thing to hash.** Rename detection (`-M`) is a similarity
heuristic; `diff.algorithm`, `core.autocrlf`, and the git version all change the bytes. Hashing
that reintroduces local/CI divergence in a new form — the exact class of bug #362 and #367 were
spent on. REQUIRED: derive the change set from TREE comparison — the sorted set of
`(path, mode, blob_sha)` over changed paths — which is config-independent and heuristic-free.

**F3 — normalization is a collision surface.** Every byte stripped to stabilise the hash is a
place two different changes hash alike. Stripping mode bits makes `chmod +x` on a hook invisible
after review. REQUIRED: mode is part of the identity; no whitespace/context normalization.

**F4 — accepting either identity scheme is a bypass.** `main` carries three `git-worktree:*`
signed entries that must keep verifying, but a gate that accepts EITHER form lets an attacker
satisfy whichever is easier. REQUIRED: the gate accepts only the form matching how IT computed
the revision for this run; an old-form entry verifies only against an old-form computation.

**F5 — `base_sha` must be gate-derived.** If the recorded base is trusted, an attacker claims a
base against which the diff is innocuous. REQUIRED: the gate derives the base itself and never
reads it from the attestation as authority.

**Also — CORRECTED 2026-07-28.** Dropping untracked files from the identity is correct for CI
(they are not in the PR) and removes the local/CI divergence trap. But P5 prosecution EXECUTES a
working tree, so an untracked test helper can change prosecution results without moving the
identity. REQUIRED (Decision 2): the local path REFUSES when untracked-and-NOT-ignored files are
present.

Note what this is NOT. The original wording — "refuses a dirty/untracked tree" — is now wrong on
the dirty half: a dirty TRACKED file is IN the identity by construction, because the current side
is computed from the working tree. There is nothing to refuse there. Only untracked-and-NOT-ignored
triggers the refusal.

## P1 adversarial review — accepted findings (2026-07-28)

A distinct-provider adversarial review of the corrected design returned `needs-attention` with six
findings; all six were judged defensible. Finding 1 is answered by Decision 2 plus the honest limit
below; finding 6 by Decision 1. The remaining three are binding implementation constraints:

**R2 — deleted paths must not reach `git hash-object`.** `--raw` still lists a deleted path, but
the file is gone from disk, so hashing or `stat`ing it crashes. REQUIRED: an explicit sentinel
(`000000` mode / 40 zeros) for the current side of a deleted path; never touch the filesystem for it.

**R3 — CRLF divergence is real; the prescribed remedy is not. SUPERSEDED 2026-07-28 by
measurement.** The finding's RISK stands: if a Windows checkout hashes CRLF where Linux CI hashes
LF, the local/CI divergence this ticket exists to remove comes back in a new form. The repo has
Windows CI legs and #352 is open on Windows breakage.

Its prescribed remedy — "mandate `git hash-object --path=<path>`" — does not address it. Measured
on git 2.x:

- `git hash-object f.txt` and `git hash-object --path=f.txt f.txt` return the **identical** hash.
  For a file already at its real working-tree path, git looks up that path's attributes either
  way; `--path=` exists for content read from stdin or from OUTSIDE the working tree.
  `--no-filters` returns a different hash, which is what proves filters were applied in both.
- What actually moves the hash is `core.autocrlf` (`false` → CRLF preserved, `true`/`input` → LF)
  — and `--path=` does not override it.
- Attributes OUTRANK `core.autocrlf`. Under a `* text=auto` rule the hash is LF for every setting
  of `core.autocrlf`.

So the real control is the repo's own `.gitattributes`, which already pins `* text=auto eol=lf`
repo-wide. ADOPTED: keep plain batched `git hash-object -- <files>` and pin the property with a
test that uses REAL CR bytes (AC16). Adopting `--path=` would additionally have forced one process
per file, since `--path` is singular and would otherwise apply one path's attributes to every file
in a batch.

**R7 — symlinks crash `hash-object`; NOT among the six review findings (found while implementing,
2026-07-28).** A symlink's blob is its TARGET PATH STRING, which is what git stores. `hash-object
<path>` opens and FOLLOWS the link, so it dies on a symlink to a DIRECTORY ("fatal: Unable to hash")
and on a dangling symlink ("could not open ... No such file or directory"). This repo tracks
`plugins/adlc-cursor/commands`, a symlink to a directory, so the case is live. Because this
primitive wraps its body in try/catch and returns null, the crash would surface as a SILENT missing
identity, not an error. REQUIRED: compute a symlink's current side from `readlink` via
`git hash-object --stdin` (no filters apply to a symlink blob); never open the path.

The legacy `resolveRevision` is not exposed to this: it pre-filters with `statSync().isFile()`,
which excludes symlinks to directories. The change-set path has no such filter and needed its own.

**R4 — base resolution must be single-sourced.** `main` vs `origin/main` vs a merge-base are three
different shas, and a local `main` that lags produces a different `base_sha` and therefore a silent
attestation-lookup failure rather than a loud error. REQUIRED: resolve the ref ONCE and pass it to
all three consumers instead of letting each derive its own.

## The honest limit — write it down, do not paper over it

Gitignored content participates in prosecution EXECUTION and sits outside EVERY identity scheme,
old and new. `node_modules` is executed by the test run and is in no revision hash on `main` today.
No hashing scheme closes this; it needs execution isolation.

Therefore: do NOT claim the identity covers what prosecution executes. Refusing on
untracked-not-ignored files (Decision 2) narrows the hole and stops this ticket from WIDENING it —
it does not close it. Execution isolation is strictly better, but it fixes a hole that PREDATES
#365. File it as its own issue; do not smuggle it in here.

## Acceptance criteria

1. An attestation for an UNCHANGED diff survives an unrelated advance of main, OR a documented
   auditable re-attestation path exists that does not require a fresh human review of an
   unchanged diff. Verify: a test rebases a fixture branch onto a new base that touches only
   unrelated files and asserts the attestation still satisfies the gate (or that the
   re-attestation path succeeds and records the carried-forward link).
2. A rebase that DOES change the diff still invalidates the attestation. Verify: a sibling
   test mutates one reviewed line and asserts the gate fails — this is the no-blanket-
   weakening guard and must be RED if criterion 1's mechanism is over-broad.
3. A same-provider or missing attestation still fails, and the distinct-provider requirement
   is unchanged. Verify: existing cross-model tests still pass unmodified.
4. ADR-0007's F4 entry is updated with the chosen resolution and its residual limits.
5. Full suite plus preflight green.


### Premortem-derived criteria

7. Identity is config-independent. Verify: a test computes the identity twice with differing git
   settings (`diff.algorithm`, rename detection, `core.autocrlf`) and asserts the value is equal —
   RED if the implementation hashes `git diff` text (F2).
8. A mode-only change (`chmod +x`) produces a DIFFERENT identity. Verify: a dedicated test — RED
   if mode is normalized away (F3).
9. Carry-forward is capped: the 4th consecutive carry-forward is refused and a fresh
   distinct-provider review is demanded; the ledger exposes chain depth. Verify: a test carries a
   verdict forward three times (each succeeding) and asserts the fourth fails closed (F1).
10. Carry-forward COMPUTES that the diff is unchanged rather than trusting an assertion. Verify:
    a test alters one reviewed byte and asserts carry-forward refuses (F1).
11. The gate does not accept a mismatched identity form. Verify: an old-form (`git-worktree:*`)
    attestation does NOT satisfy a new-form computation, and vice versa, while an old-form
    attestation still satisfies an old-form computation — the three signed entries on `main`
    keep verifying (F4).
12. `base_sha` recorded in an attestation is never used as gate authority. Verify: a test records
    an attestation naming a false base and asserts the gate still derives and uses the real one (F5).
### Basis criteria (rewritten 2026-07-28 after the reverted `base..HEAD` build)

13. The identity covers TRACKED WORKING-TREE content, not merely committed content. Verify: one
    test asserting all three — (a) an UNCOMMITTED edit to a tracked file CHANGES the identity;
    (b) reverting that edit RESTORES the original identity; (c) adding an untracked
    (non-ignored) file does NOT change the identity. RED if the implementation hashes
    `base..HEAD`. Also RED if it reads `dstsha` from `git diff --raw`: for an unstaged
    modification that field is all zeros, so every distinct working-tree content collides to one
    identity. The current side must be COMPUTED.
14. The identity basis matches the prosecution model. Verify:
    `packages/prosecute/test/prosecute-cross-model-cli.test.mjs` — `FIX A: an UNCOMMITTED edit to
    a trust-root file tiers (invisible to a committed three-dot diff)` — passes UNMODIFIED. That
    test is the acceptance signal for the basis decision. It MUST NOT be edited to accommodate the
    implementation; editing it is precisely the failure this criterion exists to catch.
15. Prosecution refuses to attest while untracked-and-NOT-ignored files are present, and the
    refusal is decided from RUNTIME-VERIFIABLE STATE rather than inferred from a hash. Verify:
    (a) a tree with one untracked non-ignored file is refused and the message names the offending
    path(s); (b) a tree whose only untracked files are GITIGNORED is NOT refused. Sub-assertion
    (b) is load-bearing: `node_modules` is gitignored and always present, so a check that triggers
    on ignored files bricks prosecution permanently.
    This criterion deliberately does NOT ask any code to distinguish "dirty tree" from "base moved"
    from "code changed" by comparing digests. A digest mismatch carries no reason, so that is
    unimplementable as stated — the same defect criticised in #364's AC5. It asks only "is the tree
    in a refusable state right now", which is directly observable.
16. Working-tree hashing is filter-normalized, so a Windows checkout agrees with Linux CI. Verify:
    a test commits content containing REAL CR bytes under a `.gitattributes` `text` rule and
    asserts the identity is UNCHANGED across `core.autocrlf` in `false`, `true` and `input`.
    The fixture content must actually contain CR — a fixture of pure-LF content passes under every
    setting and pins nothing.
    NOT "RED if `--path=` is missing": measured, `--path=` yields a byte-identical hash for a file
    at its real working-tree path (see R3). The attribute is the control, so the attribute is what
    the test pins — and the test goes red if the repo's `* text=auto eol=lf` is ever removed.
19. A SYMLINK in the change set resolves rather than silently yielding no identity. Verify: a test
    puts a symlink to a DIRECTORY into the change set (retarget it in the working tree) and a
    DANGLING symlink alongside it, and asserts the identity resolves, is `git-change:`-formed, and
    MOVES when the link is retargeted. The test must also assert `git hash-object` genuinely fails
    on that fixture, so the special case is provably load-bearing rather than decorative (R7).
17. A DELETED tracked path is representable and does not crash. Verify: a test deletes a tracked
    file and asserts the identity resolves, uses the documented sentinel (`000000` / 40 zeros) for
    the current side, and DIFFERS from the identity with the file present. RED if `git hash-object`
    or `stat` is called on a path that is gone from disk (R2).
18. Base resolution is single-sourced. Verify: a test asserts the SAME base sha reaches all three
    consumers — `record-cross-model` (writes), `tier-check` (checks), and `runProsecution` (ALSO
    checks, `packages/prosecute/lib/run.mjs:324`) — resolved ONCE and passed, not re-derived per
    consumer. RED if one resolves `main` while another resolves `origin/main` or a merge-base (R4).

## Constraints

- Do NOT weaken the distinct-provider or signature requirements; this ticket changes WHAT the
  attestation binds to, nothing else.
- Any carry-forward path must be auditable — it must be possible to see, from the ledger
  alone, that a verdict was carried forward rather than freshly reviewed, and which prior
  verdict it came from.
- Touches `packages/core/` and `packages/prosecute/` — trust-root tier, so P5 is cross-model
  gated.

## Note on sequencing

Design decision made (A+B). Next gate is P1: stress-test this design (premortem) BEFORE building
— it changes what an attestation MEANS, and a mistake here silently weakens every trust-root gate.

## Lesson for the next premortem (2026-07-28)

The P1 premortem produced five sound findings (F1–F5) and still missed the defect that forced a
revert. It attacked the identity's PROPERTIES — is it config-independent, collision-resistant,
mode-sensitive, spoofable — while ASSUMING `base..HEAD` was the right BASIS. Every finding was
correct and the thing built on top of them was still wrong, because the premise was never on trial.

Stress-test the PREMISE, not only the mechanism. A useful prompt for the next one: "what does this
identity claim to describe, and does the system actually operate on that thing?"
title: Cross-model attestation binds the whole worktree, not the reviewed diff — unrelated main activity invalidates a reviewed change (#326 F4)
